Name: Land of the Hittites
Description: The Anatolian territory of the Hittite Empire, whose people profile is the Hittite Empire entry in Ancient Civilizations, with its capital at Hattusa. This entry is the LAND, not the people: the Hittite Empire civilization entry describes the people and their empire, while this entry describes their homeland in central Anatolia. It is also not the existing Cappadocia place entry, which is a later Roman province in the same broad area, not the Bronze Age Hittite homeland. In Scripture the land of the Hittites marks the northern extent of the land promised to Israel, and Hittite kings traded with Solomon in horses and chariots.
BiblicalSignificance: The land of the Hittites shows how far the promised land's description stretched in Joshua, to a great empire far beyond Israel's borders, and how Hittites remained neighbours and trading partners of Israel from the patriarchs to Solomon.
